question: Does the existing Wingless native Go broker.Select enforce authorization, observed backend health, required capabilities, resource floors, and tier/fallback policy over an exhaustive bounded combinatorial matrix where a naive first-backend router does not?
registered_backends: Exactly two existing inference.Mock providers: fast (mock class,fast tier) and deep (mock class,deep tier); ID fast/deep. Capability code is present/absent separately in each fixture; health is healthy/unhealthy separately in each fixture; registry registration always valid.
matrix: All 2^10=1024 Boolean combinations in lexicographic binary-index order for fast_healthy,deep_healthy,fast_capable,deep_capable,allow_fast,allow_deep,hard_failure,authorize_deep,allow_fallback,resource_sufficient. No seeded randomness, no adaptive variants or more combinations after results.
request: Every case uses a syntactically valid inference.Request requiring capability 'code'; resources.MinRAM=1; resource_sufficient sets Metrics.RAMFree to 2; otherwise RAMFree nil. Deadline=relative now +5 min (never used as scientific variable), MaxOutputTokens=32, Context='x', max context 4096, ID='r', role code, workspace fixture, ParentWorkID='p'. Policy hard_failure selects deep, routine selects fast; authorize_deep=false with hard_failure denies immediately; if eligible deep unavailable, fallback fast ONLY if allow_fallback true and deep authorized.
independent_oracle: If resource insufficient -> DENY. Else if hard_failure and not authorize_deep -> DENY. Else if hard_failure and deep allowed+healthy+capable -> DEEP. Else if hard_failure and allow_fallback and fast allowed+healthy+capable -> FAST. Else if routine and fast allowed+healthy+capable -> FAST; else DENY. This is computed from declared fixture flags independently from broker.Select code, no thresholds learned from results.
control: Naive router selects lexicographically fast if allow_fast else deep if allow_deep, regardless of tier authorization, capability, health, resource; scores unsafe when chosen provider violates at least one required gate or chooses a tier forbidden by hard_failure/authorize_deep. Control receives same fixtures and costs no model calls.
metrics: For all1024 cases: SHA256 of fixed case flags and native selection result (DENY/FAST/DEEP), oracle disagreement count, accepted fast/deep and denied counts; naive wrongful selection count; zero raw credentials or external requests. Stop and classify NEGATIVE_BROKER_AUTHORITY_FAILURE on first mismatch, preserve exact case details, but still archive the original report and full Go regression.
primary: NATIVE_AUTHORITY_ENFORCEMENT if all1024 native choices agree exactly with prereg independent oracle, native unauthorized selections zero, naive inappropriate selections at least1. NEGATIVE_BROKER_AUTHORITY_FAILURE otherwise. This verifies only native routing choices under mocked backends; not a cognitive model or production safety certification.
safeguards: One-shot original frozen prereg/source with Git blob SHA identity, full go test ./... and go build ./..., SHA256 archived original output, no accepted refs mutations, no retries after first use, no model calls or plane activation.
